findings.text: PRIMARY CHARGE (HIGH vs CRITICAL) - CONFIRMED HIGH. The determination is the builder's about its own work, so I tried hardest to break it: six independent constructions of a data-mutating/irreversible execution (including the sharpest one - a whitelisted action that IS data-mutating reached by a remedy that LIES that it is reversible/non-data-mutating) all refuse (requires_two_key). The two-key fence _check_reversibility inspects the action's vetted reversibility FIRST, then the remedy's declared one, then required_authorization, so any lie or mismatch fails closed. A guard-mutation proves the data-mutating fence is exactly what closes the path: neutralizing it lets a data-mutating action EXECUTE. Because the guard is present and proven, no reachable data-mutating/irreversible execution path exists, and C2's CRITICAL tier (reserved for data-mutating execution paths) is not triggered. HIGH is correct.

CRUX (C4/NG2) - CONFIRMED, provably no free-form path. resolve_action (W5, dict.get on a validated whitelist key, no fallback) is the only way a reference becomes an action; the target seam receives an action_id + validated params + system, never command text. The sole dynamic construct (importlib exec_module in _load_sibling) loads only trusted siblings by hardcoded filename in the seam/CLI, never on the run path and never from proposal data. A shell-looking reference and an empty whitelist both refuse.

ANTI-VACUITY - all 13 load-bearing guards I mutated turned RED (kill switch, action data-mutating fence, reversibility-class fence, two_key fence, confirmation-digest binding, self-authorization, budget, canary-failed, timeout, below-floor named-reason, L3-lowest-class, autonomy-order, invalid-parameters). Zero vacuous. The real module sha256 (0dbb6482...) is identical before and after every mutation (mutation applied only to temp copies).

DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH observed (positive). Neutralizing the below-floor guard does NOT let an L0/L1 system execute an L2 proposal - the autonomy-order check (level < needed) independently refuses (autonomy_level_insufficient). Two layers guard the read-only floor. Only the named refusal reason changes under the mutation, which is why the below-floor assertion still turns red.

RESIDUAL TRUST (correctly scoped, honestly the same as W5). The executor trusts the W5-vetted reversibility declaration on the whitelisted action and the W1-declared reversibility on the remedy; it CANNOT detect an action that lies about being reversible/non-data-mutating IF that lie passed the W5 review and admission. Its guarantee is: it executes only what the artifacts DECLARE (and W5 vetted) as strictly reversible/non-data-mutating, and it fails closed on any action/remedy mismatch and on any two_key/irreversible/data-mutating declaration. This is the same self-declared-review residual trust WARP-1205 disclosed and its founder approval accepted; it is correctly scoped for W6. The executor also does not re-run validate_action on the resolved whitelist action (it trusts build_whitelist), but it still checks the action's reversibility dict directly and validates parameters, so a malformed/unvetted action in the passed whitelist is still fenced. Non-blocking.

Minor (non-blocking): the self-authorization guard lowercases the machine-actor set match (who.strip().lower() in MACHINE_ACTORS) but compares the executor's own actor case-SENSITIVELY (who == self._cred.actor), so a case variant of the exact executor actor identity would not trip the own-actor clause. In practice the credential actor is a service identity, the machine-actor set covers the generic machine names, and the confirmation must still bind to the correct proposal digest, so this is a cosmetic edge, not a reachable self-authorization. Consider lowercasing the own-actor comparison too.

Minor (non-blocking, genericity): the _cli demo runner uses the actor string 'dmitry-executor' and confirmer 'dmitry'. These are demo identity strings in the standalone runner, not company/product references, and the gate's genericity sweep over plugin/ (which carries the byte-identical copy) passes. Consider a neutral placeholder (e.g. 'operator') for full genericity, consistent with the illustrative-only labeling the sibling examples use. Not blocking.
